sections.title: AI Services for New York HR Organizations

blocks.heading: Candidate Screening and Talent Acquisition AI
paragraphs: New York's employers process enormous candidate volumes — investment banks receiving 100,000+ applications annually, media companies processing thousands of freelance and full-time applications, and NYC's tech employers competing for the same AI and software engineering talent pool. ML screening that identifies qualified candidates faster:

Resume and application parsing: NLP extracting structured candidate data from unstructured resumes, cover letters, and LinkedIn profiles — normalizing education, experience, and skills into structured profiles for comparative assessment.
Skills matching: ML matching candidate skill profiles to role requirements beyond keyword matching — semantic understanding of skill relationships and equivalences.

Candidate ranking and pipeline management: Predictive models ranking candidates by predicted qualification-to-role fit, using historical hire data and performance outcomes to calibrate ranking quality.
NYC Local Law 144 annual bias audit documentation standard for all ClickMasters NYC employment AI applications.
Cost: $45,000–$110,000 | Timeline: 10–20 weeks

blocks.heading: Workforce Analytics and Attrition Prediction
paragraphs: For New York's large enterprise employers — Citigroup, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Deloitte, McKinsey, and the major employers that define New York's workforce:

Cost: $40,000–$95,000 | Timeline: 10–18 weeks

sections.title: NYC Local Law 144: The Critical Compliance Requirement
sections.description: New York City's Local Law 144 compliance framework for automated employment decision tools.

blocks.heading: NYC Local Law 144 Requirements
paragraphs: New York City's Local Law 144, effective July 2023, requires:
Annual bias audit of any automated employment decision tool (AEDT) used for employment or promotion decisions affecting NYC candidates or employees.
The bias audit must be conducted by an independent auditor (not the AI vendor).
Public disclosure of bias audit summary on the employer's website.
Candidate notification before using an AEDT in their evaluation process.

blocks.heading: What Counts as an AEDT Under NYC LL144
paragraphs: Any computational process derived from machine learning, statistical modeling, data analytics, or AI that issues simplified output (scores, classifications, rankings) used to substantially assist or replace discretionary decision-making in employment decisions.

blocks.heading: ClickMasters' Approach to NYC LL144
paragraphs: ClickMasters designs NYC employment AI with LL144 compliance as a baseline requirement — delivering technical documentation, disparate impact test results, and audit-ready data access that the required independent bias audit will need. The annual bias audit itself is conducted by an independent auditor, not ClickMasters.
